title: Dedicated lease-window and degradation notice protocol for reserved capacity
creator: Avery Chen
description: Proposal for a customer-facing "lease-window" concept for Dedicated capacity reservations. The lease-window defines short-term (minute-level) and medium-term (hour-level) entitlements inside a contractual committed capacity. This ticket defines the definitions, measurable SLIs/SLAs, error-budget consumption rules, notification templates, and an operator playbook for graceful degradation and credit computation.
background: Customers on Dedicated purchase reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput. Incidents and short-term load spikes create ambiguity when measuring entitlement vs observed serve capacity. Current SLA language in contracts uses broad 'throughput' terms and post-fact crediting. We need a precise lease-window model that maps telemetry to contract remediation and integrates with autoscaler behavior and fleet cordoning to avoid over-allocating degraded cells.
proposal: 1) Define lease-windows: Minute-lease (60s rolling) and Hour-lease (60m rolling). Each lease-window has a guaranteed tokens-per-minute equivalent for the customer's reserved pool. 2) Measure SLI with sampled 99th-percentile served throughput per lease-window. 3) Error budget consumption: failures to meet the Minute-lease reduce a rolling Hour-lease error budget; persistent Hour-lease violations trigger formal credit events. 4) Autoscale interlock: autoscaler may burst beyond reserved pool only when lease-window headroom > 20% for 10 consecutive minutes; otherwise autoscale is limited to prevent noisy neighbor failures. 5) Fleet cordon triggers: if a zone or node group reports sustained TTI (time-to-invoke) degradation > 2x baseline for 5m, that group is cordoned from new dedicated allocations and traffic rebalanced subject to capacity policy. 6) Contract language appendices: include a short plain-English definition block plus a sample remediation table and a template credit calculation snippet.
acceptance_criteria: A concise definitions appendix exists for Minute-lease and Hour-lease and is included in the SLA annex
Telemetry mapping: a reproducible query mapping raw token service telemetry to lease-window SLI is published
Credit algorithm: a deterministic credit algorithm (pro-rata, capped) described with worked examples
Autoscale policy: knobs and thresholds documented and implementable by infra
Notification templates: notice and escalation emails for 1) minute-level transient violations 2) persistent hour-level violations
Playbook: on-call runbook for cordon/un-cordon and customer communication aligned with legal and support
metrics: Minute-lease SLI: 99p served tokens per minute vs committed tokens-per-minute
Hour-lease SLI: rolling 60-minute 95p served tokens per minute vs committed rate
Error budget burn: percentage of Hour-lease minutes where Minute-lease failed
Cordon events: count and duration per week
Autoscale burst index: number of bursts allowed vs blocked due to headroom policy
risks: Legal may require different crediting language for specific enterprise contracts
Measurement noise at low QPS customers may falsely trigger minute-lease failures without smoothing
Autoscaler changes may interact with existing burst policies and cause oscillation if thresholds are too tight
Cordoning can reduce usable capacity and create cascade failures if rebalancing is not conservative
compliance_notes: This feature touches customer contractual guarantees and telemetry used by billing reconciliation. Work with Legal and Finance to validate credit formulas and with Security for telemetry retention rules. Ensure KMS/HSM governance for any signed notices if required.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (spec): finalize lease-window and credit algorithm; get Legal signoff
Phase 1 (pilot): enable lease-window telemetry and alerts for three pilot customers on Dedicated
Phase 2 (guarded rollout): expose opt-in contractual annex for new Dedicated customers; monitor false positives
Phase 3 (general availability): default lease-window SLA language in new contracts and migrate existing customers by agreement
